correctness.rationale: PASS: The polynomial path-flux ODE is simplex-preserving, and for non-endpoint initial states the finite irreducible birth-death transport yields strict positivity at t>0. Differentiation along the tangent simplex shows gradient increments equal log(s q_{j+1}/r q_j), making each dissipation summand nonnegative with equality only at detailed balance. The stationary geometric profile q_j∝z^j and self-consistency polynomial have only z=1, plus two boundary point masses. Strict Lyapunov and connected omega-limit argument force convergence to one of the three isolated equilibria. At uniform, entropy Hessian has one negative and L-1 positive tangent directions and positive logarithmic-mean mobility, hence exactly one unstable Jacobian eigenvalue; endpoint Jacobians have strictly negative eigenvalues for L>=2. Hyperbolic asymptotic rates are orbit dependent. On M=L/2, F-F*=KL(q||uniform)>=0, so sublevel trajectories cannot cross; this proves the sufficient basin test. Independently computed k=2 uniform equilibrium Jacobian with exactly one positive and three negative eigenvalues, Hessian inertia and the rational test q=(625,375,225,135,81)/1441: M=1.0784177654 and F=0.945235672<1.163150810.

value.rationale: PASS: The incremental voter model has a natural unresolved global dynamical classification for arbitrarily many opinion levels. An explicit free-energy identity eliminates possible cycles, provides exponential trichotomy and a nontrivial rigorous basin certificate extending the previously known extreme-mean conditions. The boundary has mathematical significance even without exact separatrix or finite-population results.

final_claim: For every k>=1, the Cao–Gong 2k+1-state incremental voter mean-field ODE admits strict entropy-like Lyapunov F=sum q_j log q_j-M log M-(L-M)log(L-M)+L log L, with dissipation -sum(r q_j-s q_{j+1})log[(r q_j)/(s q_{j+1})]. All trajectories converge exponentially to left/right endpoint consensus or the unique uniform hyperbolic saddle; F<F*=L log 2-log(L+1) and the mean sign strictly determines a consensus basin.
limitations: Deterministic mean-field homogeneous fully mixed system only; no finite-agent rate or network statement.
Sublevel basin test sufficient, not exact separatrix; no uniform convergence rate across initial data.
